requirement: Prove checkpoint restore creates a safe recovery point first when possible and never blind-overwrites newer unrelated work.
invariants: Restore planning binds both working VFS generation and canonical OPFS sequence/generation.
A VFS mutation lease blocks local transaction publication during the restore commit window.
Current working state is persisted or reused as a recovery point before older checkpoint content is published.
Restored content is published as a new canonical generation; canonical generation identity never moves backward.
Local work created after restore planning aborts with OC_STALE_GENERATION.
Cross-context canonical publication after planning aborts with OC_STALE_GENERATION.
Quota failure before the safety point aborts with OC_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, riskDeclared=true, and no working-tree mutation.
The recovery point remains a retained fallback after restored-generation reopen.
